subject: Predictable p99 for a multi-region data layer
body:
Hi Tom,

I see the Northwind Payments team is focused on capacity planning and on evaluating cost and latency improvements for its multi-region data layer, alongside the Kafka estate.

If tail latency is part of that evaluation, here is one data point: ScyllaDB uses a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 latency stays predictable under load.

Would a short technical write-up on how that architecture behaves be useful for your evaluation?

Oz

subject: Cassandra leaderboard p99 and GC pauses
body:
Hi Lior,

subject: Fraud scoring throughput across three regions
body:
Hi Maya, thanks for connecting.

I saw that Northwind Payments runs fraud scoring on Astra DB, with single-digit millisecond reads across three regions at 40k transactions per second. That is a demanding profile to keep cost-efficient as volume grows.

ScyllaDB is built for that kind of workload. Higher throughput per node typically means fewer nodes and lower infrastructure cost. With DataStax now part of IBM, this may also be a reasonable moment to review options.

Would you be open to comparing notes on how your fraud-scoring cluster is sized today?
